outcomeNote: A mishna stating law with no dispute, no named tanna and no adduced source; the gemara's questioning of these clauses begins in the following unit.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַכֹּל מַעֲרִיכִין, וְנֶעֱרָכִין, נוֹדְרִין וְנִידָּרִין — כֹּהֲנִים, לֹוִים וְיִשְׂרְאֵלִים, נָשִׁים וַעֲבָדִים.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» «Everyone takes» vows of «valuation» and is thereby obligated to donate to the Temple treasury the value fixed by the Torah (see Leviticus 27:3–7) for the age and sex of the person valuated. «And» similarly, everyone «is valuated,» and therefore one who vowed to donate his fixed value is obligated to pay. Likewise, everyone «vows» to donate to the Temple treasury the assessment of a person, based on his market value to be sold as a slave, and is thereby obligated to pay; «and» everyone is the object of «a vow» if others vowed to donate his assessment. This includes «priests, Levites and Israelites, women, and» Canaanite «slaves.»

segments.he: טוּמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס, נוֹדְרִין וְנִידָּרִין וּמַעֲרִיכִין, אֲבָל לֹא נֶעֱרָכִין, שֶׁאֵינוֹ נֶעֱרָךְ אֶלָּא הַזָּכָר וַדַּאי וּנְקֵבָה וַדָּאִית.
segments.en: «A tumtum,» whose sexual organs are concealed, «and a hermaphrodite [androginos], vow, and» are the object of «a vow, and take» vows of «valuation, but they are not valuated.» Consequently, if one says, with regard to a tumtum: The valuation of so-and-so is incumbent upon me to donate to the Temple treasury, he is not obligated to pay anything, «as only a definite male or a definite female are valuated.»

segments.he: חֵרֵשׁ שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן נִידָּרִין וְנֶעֱרָכִין, אֲבָל לֹא נוֹדְרִין וְלֹא מַעֲרִיכִין, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם דַּעַת.
segments.en: «A deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor» are the object of «a vow and are valuated, but neither vow» to donate the assessment of a person «nor take» a vow of «valuation, because they lack the» presumed «mental competence» to make a commitment.

moves.summary: the mishna states the general inclusion: everyone, of every class and both sexes, valuates, is valuated, vows and is vowed
the mishna qualifies the general clause: one of indeterminate or double sex is not valuated, since valuation applies only to a definite male or female
the mishna qualifies the general clause in the other direction: those lacking legal competence can be valuated and vowed about but cannot themselves vow
